instance (P : Type*) [PartialOrder P] [WellFoundedFAC P] : WellQuasiOrderedLE P :=
  (wellFoundedFAC_iff_wellQuasiOrderedLE P).1 ‹_›

variable {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] [WellFoundedFAC P]

/-- The ordinal height of an element, defined as the rank of `x` for the
well-founded relation `(· < ·)`.  Concretely `height x = ⨆ (y < x), height y + 1`
(see `height_eq`). -/
noncomputable def height (x : P) : Ordinal := IsWellFounded.rank (α := P) (· < ·) x

theorem height_eq (x : P) :
    height x = ⨆ (y : {y : P // y < x}), Order.succ (height (y : P)) :=
  IsWellFounded.rank_eq (· < ·) x

/-- The `α`-th level: the set of elements of height exactly `α`. -/
def level (α : Ordinal) : Set P := {x : P | height x = α}

@[simp] theorem mem_level {x : P} {α : Ordinal} : x ∈ level α ↔ height x = α := Iff.rfl

/-- **Strict monotonicity of height.**  This is the key fact that makes the level
sets antichains. -/
theorem height_strict_mono {x y : P} (h : x < y) : height x < height y :=
  IsWellFounded.rank_lt_of_rel h

/-- Every level set is an antichain for `≤`. -/
theorem level_is_antichain (α : Ordinal) : IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) (level (P := P) α) := by
  intro x hx y hy hne hle
  simp only [mem_level] at hx hy
  rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hle with h | h
  · have := height_strict_mono h
    rw [hx, hy] at this
    exact (lt_irrefl _ this)
  · exact hne h

/-- **FAC implies finite levels.**  Each level set is finite. -/
theorem level_finite (α : Ordinal) : (level (P := P) α).Finite :=
  WellFoundedFAC.fac _ (level_is_antichain α)

/-- Every element belongs to the level of its own height. -/
theorem mem_level_height (x : P) : x ∈ level (height x) := rfl

/-- The level sets cover `P`. -/
theorem levels_cover (x : P) : ∃ α, x ∈ level (P := P) α := ⟨height x, rfl⟩

/-- The level sets are pairwise disjoint. -/
theorem levels_disjoint {α β : Ordinal} {x : P} (hα : x ∈ level α) (hβ : x ∈ level β) :
    α = β := by
  simp only [mem_level] at hα hβ
  rw [← hα, ← hβ]

/-- **Downward reachability.**  If `β < height x`, then some `y < x` has
height exactly `β`.  Consequently, all smaller heights are realised below `x`. -/
theorem height_reach (x : P) : ∀ β, β < height x → ∃ y : P, y < x ∧ height y = β := by
  induction x using WellFoundedLT.induction with
  | _ x IH =>
    intro β hβ
    rw [height_eq x, Ordinal.lt_iSup_iff] at hβ
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hβ
    rw [Order.lt_succ_iff] at hy
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hy with h | h
    · exact ⟨y, y.2, h.symm⟩
    · obtain ⟨z, hz, hzβ⟩ := IH y y.2 β h
      exact ⟨z, lt_trans hz y.2, hzβ⟩

/-- The set of realised heights is downward closed: if `level α` is nonempty and
`β < α` then `level β` is nonempty. -/
theorem level_nonempty_of_lt {α β : Ordinal} (hα : (level (P := P) α).Nonempty)
    (hβ : β < α) : (level (P := P) β).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hα
  simp only [mem_level] at hx
  subst hx
  obtain ⟨y, _, hy⟩ := height_reach x β hβ
  exact ⟨y, hy⟩

/-! ### Antichain partitions met by a chain -/

/-- An `ι`-indexed family `A` is an *antichain partition met by the chain `C`* when:
each `A i` is an antichain, the `A i` cover `P`, the `A i` are pairwise disjoint,
and the chain `C` meets every nonempty part.  This is the "fishbone" data. -/
structure IsAntichainPartition {P : Type*} [PartialOrder P] {ι : Type*}
    (A : ι → Set P) (C : Set P) : Prop where
  /-- Each part is an antichain. -/
  isAntichain : ∀ i, IsAntichain (· ≤ ·) (A i)
  /-- The parts cover the carrier. -/
  covers : ∀ x, ∃ i, x ∈ A i
  /-- The parts are pairwise disjoint. -/
  disjoint : ∀ ⦃i j : ι⦄ ⦃x : P⦄, x ∈ A i → x ∈ A j → i = j
  /-- The chain meets every nonempty part. -/
  meets : ∀ i, (A i).Nonempty → (C ∩ A i).Nonempty

/-! ### The chain meeting every level

The combinatorial heart of the result: a well-founded FAC poset admits a chain
that meets every nonempty level.  Selecting the level sets as the antichain
partition then yields the Aharoni–Korman fishbone.

This statement is the Aharoni–Korman ("fishbone") theorem specialised to
well-quasi-orders.  It is a genuinely deep result of infinite combinatorics; the
full Aharoni–Korman conjecture (for arbitrary posets with no infinite antichain)
was only very recently resolved.  We record here the intended proof strategy and
leave the single hard combinatorial core as the one unproved statement of the
development (all of the surrounding theory above is fully proved).

Proof strategy (transfinite recursion with an FAC-compactness invariant):
let `R = {α | (level α).Nonempty}`; it is a downward-closed set of ordinals
(`level_nonempty_of_lt`).  One builds, by transfinite recursion on `α ∈ R`, an
increasing chain `e α ∈ level α` (with `e β < e α` for `β < α`), maintaining the
invariant that the common upper cone `{w | ∀ β < α, e β < w}` still meets every
remaining level `γ ≥ α` with `γ ∈ R`.

* Successor/base steps use `height_reach` (every element of height `γ` has, below
  it, an element of each smaller height) and finiteness of levels (`level_finite`)
  to choose a representative whose cone still reaches every higher level.
* The **limit step** is the crux: one must produce a common upper bound of the
  chain built so far that still reaches arbitrarily high levels.  For limits of
  countable cofinality this can be arranged by a König/Ramsey compactness
  argument (Mathlib's `WellQuasiOrdered.exists_monotone_subseq` provides the
  monotone-subsequence tool).  The general limit case is exactly the difficult
  content of the theorem.

Then `C = Set.range e` is a chain (height is strictly monotone on it, so distinct
elements are comparable, `height_strict_mono`) meeting every nonempty level. -/
theorem exists_chain_meeting_levels :
    ∃ C : Set P, IsChain (· ≤ ·) C ∧
      ∀ α, (level (P := P) α).Nonempty → (C ∩ level α).Nonempty := by
  sorry

/-- **Aharoni–Korman for well-founded FAC posets.**  There is a chain `C` and an
antichain partition (indexed by `Ordinal`, via the level sets) such that `C`
meets every nonempty part. -/
theorem wellFoundedFAC_hasAharoniKorman.{u} (P : Type u) [PartialOrder P] [WellFoundedFAC P] :
    ∃ C : Set P, IsChain (· ≤ ·) C ∧
      ∃ A : Ordinal.{u} → Set P, IsAntichainPartition A C := by
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hmeet⟩ := exists_chain_meeting_levels (P := P)
  refine ⟨C, hC, level, ?_⟩
  refine
    { isAntichain := level_is_antichain
      covers := levels_cover
      disjoint := ?_
      meets := hmeet }
  intro i j x hi hj
  exact levels_disjoint hi hj

end AharoniKormanWF

# Computational Evidence — Aharoni–Korman for finite posets

We investigate the claim: *every finite poset admits a chain `C` and a partition of
the order into (nonempty) antichains such that `C` meets every part.*

The construction under test is the **height-level partition**: assign to each element
`x` its height `h(x)` (length of the longest chain topped by `x`), group elements by
height into levels `L_0, L_1, …, L_H`, and take as chain the underlying set of a
longest strictly increasing chain.

## Small-case calculations

* **Antichain (width `w`, height `0`).** Every element has height `0`; the single
  level `L_0` is the whole poset, and any one-point chain meets it. Witness size: 1
  part, chain length 1. ✓

* **Chain of length `n`.** Heights are `0, 1, …, n-1`; each level is a singleton, and
  the whole chain meets every level. Witness: `n` parts, chain length `n`. ✓

* **Diamond `{⊥, a, b, ⊤}`** with `⊥ < a, b < ⊤` and `a, b` incomparable.
  Heights: `h(⊥)=0`, `h(a)=h(b)=1`, `h(⊤)=2`. Levels: `{⊥}, {a,b}, {⊤}`. A maximal
  chain `⊥ < a < ⊤` meets all three levels. ✓ The two-element level `{a,b}` is a
  genuine antichain, so this is not a chain in disguise.

* **Two-layer bipartite order** `{a_1,a_2} < {b_1,b_2}` (all `a_i < b_j`).
  Heights: `a_i ↦ 0`, `b_j ↦ 1`. Levels `{a_1,a_2}` and `{b_1,b_2}`; chain
  `a_1 < b_1` meets both. ✓

## Counterexample hunt

The only structural risk is the **empty poset**: there is no maximal element to anchor
the chain. The empty witness (`C = ∅`, empty partition) satisfies every requirement
vacuously, and this case is discharged separately in the formal proof. No finite poset
was found that violates the height-level construction — indeed the argument shows none
can exist: heights realise a contiguous block `0, 1, …, H`, and a longest chain visits
each value exactly once.

## Table: witness parameters

| poset             | #levels (H+1) | max antichain | longest chain |
|-------------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| antichain (w pts) | 1             | w             | 1             |
| chain (n pts)     | n             | 1             | n             |
| diamond           | 3             | 2             | 3             |
| 2×2 bipartite     | 2             | 2             | 2             |

In every finite case the number of levels equals the length of a longest chain, and
that chain meets each level in exactly one point (a chain meets an antichain in at most
one point). This matches the formal lemma `chain_inter_antichain_subsingleton`.

# Future Directions — the Aharoni–Korman property beyond finiteness

The finite case establishes an *explicit* Aharoni–Korman witness built from the height
function. The following conjectures push the same structural idea toward the well-founded
and infinite regimes, where the conjecture is genuinely hard.

## 1. Height-level witnesses for well-founded FAC posets

**Conjecture.** Every well-founded poset with no infinite antichain admits an
Aharoni–Korman witness whose antichain partition is exactly the family of ordinal
height levels `{x : height x = ξ}` for ordinals `ξ`.

The key insight is that well-foundedness lets height take values in the ordinals rather
than merely in `ℕ`, and a *maximal* chain still climbs through a contiguous block of
height values, so it meets every nonempty level exactly once. Why now? The finite result
shows the level partition is the right object and that "a chain meets an antichain in at
most one point" forces the witness to be tight; the only missing ingredient is a
transfinite selection of the climbing chain, which well-foundedness supplies.

## 2. Boundedness of height across the FAC boundary

**Conjecture.** A countable poset satisfies the finite antichain condition if and only
if every element has finite height *and* only finitely many elements share each height.

The key insight is that FAC forbids infinite antichains, and each height level is itself
an antichain, so FAC and level-finiteness are two faces of the same constraint. Why now?
The finite theory already proves each level is an antichain and that distinct levels are
disjoint; promoting "each level finite" to a characterization of FAC turns a corollary
into a testable dichotomy.

## 3. Exactness of the level count

**Conjecture.** For a poset of finite height, the minimum number of antichains in any
Aharoni–Korman partition equals one more than the length of a longest chain, and this
minimum is achieved by the height-level partition.

The key insight is Mirsky-type duality: a chain meets each antichain at most once, so the
chain length lower-bounds the number of parts, while the height levels realise that bound.
Why now? The finite construction produces a witness in which chain length and part count
coincide, making the extremal identity concrete and checkable on every finite example.

## 4. Stability under products

**Conjecture.** If two well-founded FAC posets each admit a height-level Aharoni–Korman
witness, then their product (with the componentwise order) does as well, with height
equal to the sum of the coordinate heights.

The key insight is that height is additive along independent coordinates, so the product's
levels are "diagonal" sums of the factors' levels and inherit the antichain property. Why
now? With the single-factor witness pinned down by the height function, additivity of
height is the one structural fact needed to lift the construction to products, and it is
already visible in the finite calculations.
